lead: >-
  Argentina, Bolivia and Uruguay come together on one extended Ada Tours journey through six South American countries. Culinary experiences differ considerably: dinner with Argentine wine accompanies a tango show in Buenos Aires, Montevideo introduces Uruguayan culture, and in Bolivia's highlands the Uyuni Salt Flat and the practical demands of expedition travel take center stage. A winery excursion in Chile is offered as an optional activity. Here we examine the actual itinerary without inventing tastings in every country.
---

## Argentina, Bolivia and Uruguay: how the culinary itinerary works

**Our collection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with Argentina, Bolivia and Uruguay among the journey's principal countries.** It features the [20-day Six Countries of Latin America tour: from Rio to Machu Picchu](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/). In addition to the selected three, it visits Brazil, Chile and Peru. Rest time, flights and excursions span several climate zones, from coastal metropolises to high-altitude Bolivia.

The trip suits travelers who want to combine South America's landmark destinations with local cuisine and occasional food-focused evenings. However, **the Food and Wine interest label does not mean daily tastings, wineries in every country or included culinary workshops**. Before booking, examine the actual itinerary to see which experiences are included and which are offered for an additional fee.

The [general Argentina–Bolivia–Uruguay catalog](/multi-country/argentina_bolivia_uruguay/) shows tours without limiting the selection to food and wine. For more specialized journeys with dedicated tastings and winery visits, see the [culinary tours section](/interests/food-and-wine/).

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_latin_america_six_countries_20_days_2026}}

## Argentina: Buenos Aires, tango and dinner with wine

The Argentine stage includes [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), a city of broad avenues, historic neighborhoods and evening tango performances. The itinerary includes walks through key districts and **a tango show with dinner**. The stated menu features several traditional dishes accompanied by Argentine wines. This is a confirmed culinary experience that can genuinely inform your choice of tour.

Here, food is inseparable from city culture: dinner takes place during a performance in which music and dance matter as much as the dishes. Travelers whose main goal is to explore Argentina's wine regions should understand the distinction. A wine dinner in Buenos Aires is not the same as a dedicated excursion to Mendoza, including vineyards, cellars and a meeting with a winemaker.

Such visits can be considered as a separate extension if desired, with dates, flights and accommodation recalculated. They cannot be assumed part of the published itinerary just because Argentina is associated with wine and Malbec grapes.

## Uruguay: Montevideo and an introduction to local culture

The Uruguay section includes a stop in [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) with an introductory sightseeing program. It covers the port, Independence Square, the old city and the cathedral. This is an opportunity to experience the capital on the Río de la Plata and appreciate how Uruguay's largest city differs from neighboring Buenos Aires.

Uruguay is known for Tannat wine, meat dishes and the asado cooking tradition. These can be appealing culinary themes for a longer visit. However, on this six-country tour **a visit to a Uruguayan winery or a dedicated tasting in Montevideo is not listed among the included services**. Wine activities absent from the itinerary should be treated only as separately arranged options.

This is a good place to set your priorities: use the single day for a historical city tour or extend your stay for restaurants and wine estates. Adding a culinary event means allowing for transport, winery opening hours and possible changes to all subsequent travel arrangements.

## Bolivia: Uyuni, lagoons and food in the highlands

The Bolivian section is fundamentally different from the urban evenings in Argentina and Uruguay. The route crosses the Andean highlands, lagoons, geysers and the [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). Four-wheel-drive journeys and an overnight stay under expedition conditions are part of the program. Travelers then reach La Paz for a sightseeing tour of the city and its historic neighborhoods.

Bolivian cuisine has its own regional ingredients and dishes, but here **meal logistics during long journeys** take precedence. Travel across the highlands rarely resembles a restaurant itinerary: mealtimes depend on stops, weather and distances. The program mentions a boxed lunch. That is a confirmed part of the trip, but should not be turned into a promise of a tasting menu.

At altitude, gradual adjustment, hydration and individual well-being are important. The route includes high-altitude sections, so health considerations should be discussed with a doctor before traveling. Travelers with special dietary requirements should also confirm in advance which meals can be provided at hotels and on drives across the plateau. **An expedition overnight stay does not offer the same range of restaurants as Buenos Aires.**

Adding a Bolivian wine region or culinary activity would require a separate plan. Such an experience is not advertised in the ready-made itinerary and cannot be inferred from its general Food and Wine classification.

## Where a winery visit is actually available on the trip

Another wine-related experience takes place in Chile, even though the country is **not among the three selected in this filter**. After the visit to Santiago, the program mentions **an optional excursion to wineries in the Maipo Valley with a tasting**. It costs extra, so allow for it in your budget and arrange the timing in advance. A winery visit must not be described as a guaranteed part of the basic package.

It helps to distinguish three levels of culinary involvement:

| Experience | Status on this tour |
|---|---|
| Dinner with wine at the Argentine tango show | Listed in the itinerary |
| Maipo Valley wineries in Chile | Optional, for an additional charge |
| Wineries in Uruguay or Bolivia | No separate visits advertised |

This distinction helps avoid disappointment when a traveler expects a dedicated wine tour but joins a busy six-country sightseeing itinerary where a tasting is only one possible episode.

If vineyards are your top priority, choose a trip with several wineries confirmed in advance, along with time for production tours and tastings. If your main goal is South America from Rio to Machu Picchu, the food experiences on this program complement the wider exploration.

## Price, seasons and flights between countries

The ready-made tour lasts 20 days, with domestic flights and accommodation as specified in the itinerary. Different rates apply for double and single occupancy, and international flights are paid separately. Confirm the included services, prices of optional experiences and actual departure dates on the [current tour page](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) before deciding. Do not automatically carry dates from one departure into the following season.

The weather changes as you move through the countries. Buenos Aires and Montevideo have a more temperate climate than tropical Brazil, while the Bolivian mountains require warm clothing even on sunny days. Changes in altitude, domestic flights and hotel changes determine the time available for additional restaurants or tastings.

Payment arrangements also matter. Argentina uses the Argentine peso, Uruguay the Uruguayan peso, and Bolivia the boliviano. Card acceptance depends on the country, bank and payment infrastructure; **bank cards issued in Russia may not work abroad**. Arrange several lawful payment options and small amounts of cash for incidental expenses along the route.

Because the itinerary crosses six countries, entry and transit requirements must be checked separately for each traveler's citizenship and dates. Discuss possible contraindications and an acclimatization plan with a doctor before the high-altitude sections. An optional Chilean tasting must also fit around later flights without creating schedule conflicts.

## Frequently asked questions about culinary journeys through Argentina, Bolivia and Uruguay

### Is there a ready-made trip visiting only these three countries?

This collection shows one 20-day itinerary through six countries, including Brazil, Chile and Peru. A custom journey limited to Argentina, Bolivia and Uruguay would require a separate program.

### Are wine tastings included in each of the three countries?

No. In Argentina, the program includes dinner with local wines during the tango show. Dedicated winery excursions in Uruguay and Bolivia are not advertised.

### Can I visit wineries in Chile?

The itinerary offers an optional tasting excursion to the Maipo Valley at additional cost. Its timing, availability and price must be arranged separately.

### Is the program suitable for a leisurely culinary holiday?

It is an intensive six-country sightseeing itinerary with many journeys, including Bolivia's highlands. For a slower holiday with several restaurant evenings and winery visits, choose a smaller geographical area or extend selected stops.

### Does altitude matter on the Bolivian section?

Yes. The itinerary includes high-altitude journeys and an expedition-style overnight stay. Discuss your health and altitude tolerance with a doctor before departure; generic travel advice cannot replace individual medical guidance.

## Argentina, Bolivia and Uruguay: where the nature experiences take place

Here you will find {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} through Argentina, Bolivia and Uruguay with a Nature theme. Both current Ada Tours programs extend beyond this trio: the [20-day six-country tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) also visits Brazil, Chile and Peru, while the [32-day eight-country itinerary](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) continues to Ecuador and Colombia.

The three countries offer completely different experiences. Argentina has [Iguazú Falls](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) and the surrounding rainforest. Bolivia offers [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/), colorful lagoons, volcanic landscapes and high-altitude roads. Uruguay appears as a visit to [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) from Buenos Aires; these tours do not advertise a full expedition into a Uruguayan national park.

This distinction matters if you are traveling primarily for nature. A short city trip to Montevideo adds value to the itinerary, but cannot be counted as the equivalent of an Iguazú day or a drive across Bolivia's plateau. General travel and visa considerations are covered by the [Argentina–Bolivia–Uruguay catalog](/multi-country/argentina_bolivia_uruguay/). Below, we focus on the nature experiences themselves.

## Argentina: Iguazú and the forest of Misiones

On both tours, Argentina's nature section centers on [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/). The Argentine side of Iguazú Falls lies here, surrounded by humid Atlantic rainforest. The national park is known for its extensive viewing paths running alongside different branches of the river and its cascades. The trip also includes the Brazilian side of the falls: two different banks and two separate protected areas.

From Brazil, you can appreciate the scale of the waterfalls in a broad panorama; from Argentina, forest paths bring you closer to individual cascades. Visiting both parks takes time for transfers and an international border crossing. Water levels and weather can affect access to particular areas, so avoid adding unnecessary journeys to this part of the trip.

Iguazú is an excellent example of a natural attraction that should not automatically be described as a wildlife safari. The forest is rich in biodiversity, but the primary purpose of these days in both programs is to see the waterfalls. Encounters with particular animals or birds are not guaranteed. For a different objective, see the [nature and wildlife tours](/interests/wildlife/), where the actual arrangements for watching animals should be compared.

After Iguazú, travelers move to Buenos Aires. This is an urban stage, so assess the proportion of genuine nature days separately from the number of attractions visited in the capital.

## Bolivia: the most dramatic change of landscape and altitude

The Bolivian section of both itineraries follows the Chilean stop in San Pedro de Atacama. A high-altitude journey by 4×4 vehicles begins. The itinerary lists [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/), volcanic views near Licancabur, the Dalí Desert, the Polques hot springs, the Sol de Mañana geothermal area, [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/) and the [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/).

There is none of Iguazú's lush greenery here. Travelers reach an open highland plateau of salt flats, lagoons in different shades, winds and sharp temperature changes. Bolivia's tourism portal places the salt-flat area at around 3,660 meters, while some route sections are above 4,000 meters. The 32-day itinerary explicitly mentions the possibility of altitude-related discomfort.

Altitude is the main practical issue, and choosing an attractive photograph does not solve it. Even ordinary walking can feel different from walking at sea level. The itinerary includes a stop in San Pedro de Atacama before the crossing, but this does not guarantee freedom from an individual response to altitude. People with conditions affecting their tolerance for high elevations should seek medical advice beforehand.

The season also changes the appearance of Uyuni. During wetter periods, water on parts of the salt surface can reflect the sky; in the dry season, the salt flat's own textures are more visible. However, **a mirror effect cannot be guaranteed on any particular date**. Rain affects the passability of some areas, so four-wheel-drive routes depend on actual road conditions.

Finally, Laguna Colorada, Laguna Verde and the salt flat are not all one viewpoint. Driving stages between them take time. If you want to observe and photograph the scenery at a relaxed pace, preserving a full Bolivian section makes more sense than artificially shortening it to add city stops.

## Uruguay: a Montevideo visit, not a separate wilderness expedition

Both programs include **a day trip from Buenos Aires to Montevideo**. The 32-day tour explicitly mentions an early transfer to the port, a ferry crossing, sightseeing and an evening return to Argentina; ferry tickets are included. The 20-day trip also describes Montevideo as a separate day reached by river.

It is an important break between two natural regions, but the excursion is predominantly urban: the port, historic districts and an introduction to Uruguay. The shore of the Río de la Plata provides an attractive geographical backdrop, but **the tour includes no confirmed multi-day nature itinerary in Uruguay**.

Replacing a Montevideo sightseeing day with a longer nature stay in Uruguay would mean changing the itinerary, not activating a feature already included in the package. The ferry, subsequent flights and number of days would all need to be coordinated again. On current programs, regard this day as a contrast between cities and natural regions without expecting it to be a dedicated nature experience.

## Comparing the two programs: 20 or 32 days

| Itinerary | Nature highlights |
|---|---|
| [6 countries, 20 days](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) | Both sides of Iguazú, high-altitude lagoons and Uyuni; Montevideo as a city day |
| [8 countries, 32 days](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) | The same key regions, extended through Ecuador with the Galápagos and Colombia |

When comparing **only the natural sites of Argentina, Bolivia and Uruguay**, both programs share a similar core. The difference is how many additional countries and nature experiences you want after Peru. The 32-day journey adds Ecuador and the Galápagos Islands: a separate nature stage in another country, not an additional Uruguayan excursion.

If Iguazú and Uyuni are your principal goals, start with the 20-day option and examine its actual dates, terms and physical demands. If you want a much longer journey with new natural regions, consider the 32-day route. Each program has its own schedule and services, which should not be transferred from one tour to the other by analogy.

{{#if catalog.hasComparableUsdPrice}}
The lowest comparable published price in this collection is {{catalog.minUsdPriceLabel}}. Compare the included flights and accommodation as well before deciding.
{{/if}}

## Weather, luggage and health on a contrasting itinerary

The main challenge is moving from warm, humid Iguazú to the dry and cold highlands. A waterproof layer and shoes with good grip are useful at the waterfalls; for Bolivia, pack a warm jacket and protection against wind, sun and dry air. Plan your luggage around the allowances on all domestic flights, not just your international baggage.

The itinerary also follows different seasonal conditions. Water levels and trail access at Iguazú do not follow the same pattern as seasonal road conditions on the salt flat. Promising perfect weather in both regions would be misleading. Plan around your main nature objective and confirmed transport connections between countries.

Because of Bolivia's altitude, assess your physical condition, possible health restrictions and the time available to acclimatize. The Uruguay day, by contrast, is mainly about the ferry schedule and border formalities. These are different requirements even though all three countries appear in the same multi-country journey.

## Frequently asked questions about nature in Argentina, Bolivia and Uruguay

### Where are the strongest nature experiences on these tours?

Within the selected trio, Argentina's principal natural attraction is Iguazú Falls, while Bolivia offers the longest high-altitude section with lagoons and the Uyuni Salt Flat.

### Is there a separate nature itinerary in Uruguay?

Not on the two programs discussed. Montevideo is visited for one day of city sightseeing; adding a nature-focused stay in Uruguay would require a separate itinerary change.

### How high are the Bolivian lagoon routes?

The Uyuni Salt Flat lies at about 3,660 meters, while some sections of the high-altitude lagoon route exceed 4,000 meters. Individual altitude tolerance must be considered.

### Can Uyuni's mirror reflection be guaranteed?

No. The reflection requires water on the salt surface and suitable conditions. Weather also affects road access and the exact four-wheel-drive route.

### What makes the 32-day tour different from the 20-day tour for nature lovers?

Both include Iguazú and Bolivia's lagoons. The 32-day route adds natural regions, notably the Galápagos Islands in Ecuador.

### Can I replace the Montevideo day with an extra day in Bolivia?

Only by changing the itinerary and checking ferry arrangements, subsequent flights and the overland schedule. That change is not automatically included in the published conditions.

## Three countries on a wider itinerary with Galápagos wildlife watching

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. Argentina, Bolivia and Uruguay are principal countries on the 32-day journey, while included animal-watching excursions take place in Ecuador's Galápagos. Natural stops in the selected trio and dedicated wildlife excursions elsewhere on the full route serve different purposes.

In [Argentina](/argentina/), the main natural stage of these tours is the [Argentine side of Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/). Paths and viewing platforms allow visitors to see the cascades and surrounding rainforest. Iguazú National Park protects part of the Paraná Atlantic Forest, home to toucans, coatis and many other animals. This is a nature excursion focused on waterfalls; no encounter with a particular animal species is guaranteed by the itinerary.

In [Bolivia](/bolivia/), the nature section takes two consecutive days of off-road travel. [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/) is known for high-altitude flamingos, including James's flamingo, which is mentioned in the excursion description. Travelers then continue past the Honda, Hedionda, Chiarkota and Cañapa lagoons, volcanic scenery and the [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). These places are rewarding landscapes even when birds are far from the road.

[Uruguay](/uruguay/) is represented by [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/): city sightseeing, the port, central districts and a return ferry to Argentina. This section does not include a national park, whale watching or a dedicated wildlife excursion. Uruguay is part of the country combination but does not contribute a standalone wildlife program.

## How Iguazú differs from Bolivia's high-altitude lagoons

| Location | Main experience |
|---|---|
| Iguazú | Waterfalls, humid forest |
| Laguna Colorada | High-altitude lake, possible flamingos |
| Uyuni | Salt-flat landscape |
| Montevideo | City sightseeing |

Iguazú is a subtropical natural area. The Argentine national park's official website describes its humid climate, varied forest communities and abundant wildlife. Even without seeing a toucan or coati, a walk around the waterfalls remains a rich nature experience. Spray, the condition of individual paths and access to platforms nevertheless depend on actual conditions.

The Bolivian Altiplano is quite different: the air is thin, open spaces offer little protection against the wind, and distances between lagoons are long. The itinerary uses 4×4 jeeps with stops. Birds use different lagoons at different times, so the presence of flamingos in the region cannot be turned into a promise of a close sighting at a predetermined hour.

A useful feature of the combination is the opportunity to compare **the humid Iguazú forest with the cold high-altitude ecosystems of Bolivia** on one long journey. If nature is your priority, this contrast matters more than listing three countries in the title.

## The difference between a nature trip and a wildlife-watching tour

For a nature-focused comparison, look at [Six Countries of Latin America in 20 Days](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/). That tour belongs to the Nature category: it includes Iguazú and a two-day jeep route in Bolivia, but no separate wildlife-watching activity is identified on those days. Between these stages are Buenos Aires, a one-day Montevideo visit and Chile. After Uyuni, the group continues through La Paz to Peru. This option moves quickly between landscapes; possible bird sightings at the lagoons are part of a varied scenic journey.

[Eight Countries of South America in 32 Days](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) covers similar highlights in Argentina, Uruguay and Bolivia, but continues through Peru, Ecuador and Colombia. The longer itinerary includes a sea excursion in Ecuador's Galápagos Islands: North Seymour and Bachas or South Plaza and Carrion Point. The option is confirmed after booking. Birds, sea lions and other island wildlife are observed **outside the selected three countries**, providing the basis for classifying the whole trip under Wildlife Watching. Galápagos animals must not be attributed to the Argentine, Bolivian or Uruguayan stages.

The table below compares programs with included wild-animal or birdwatching opportunities. Scenic trips without such activities can be compared in the [nature journeys collection](/multi-country/argentina_bolivia_uruguay/interests/nature/). On a multi-country tour, wildlife watching may take place outside the countries mentioned in the collection title: check the complete itinerary and the exact days.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

If flamingos and high-altitude landscapes are your main priority, the [Bolivia nature tours collection](/interests/nature/tours/bolivia/) will help you compare options. For other wildlife-focused travel, see the [general Wildlife Watching interest](/interests/wildlife/) and [multi-country wildlife-watching tours](/multi-country/interests/wildlife/).

## Why wildlife watching requires spare time

Two days around Bolivia's lagoons combine journeys on remote roads, stops in geothermal areas and visits to salt flats. Time at any particular lagoon is limited by the overall schedule. Birds move freely between lakes, and close observation is possible only under suitable conditions and in compliance with local rules.

In Argentina, most excursion time is devoted to the waterfalls. Bird and animal enthusiasts should identify their preference in advance: walking along standard Iguazú trails, spending additional hours observing wildlife or booking a specialized excursion with a naturalist guide are different products. **The last option is not confirmed as included** on these particular itineraries and requires separate discussion.

In protected natural areas, stay on designated trails, keep your distance from wildlife and do not feed animals. A telephoto lens or binoculars can be helpful for photography, but these programs do not provide such equipment as a guaranteed inclusion. We can discuss which style of wildlife watching matters most and what schedule adjustments may be arranged, without promising a wildlife encounter.

## Seasons, altitude and luggage: what may affect the trip

An itinerary linking Iguazú with Bolivia combines very different weather. Around Iguazú, the air is warmer and more humid, with possible rain and slippery, damp trails. On the Bolivian plateau, visitors need protection from wind, cold and strong sun, plus clothing suitable for rapid changes during the day.

Some sections of the Bolivian jeep tour are above 4,000 meters. Altitude and acclimatization matter even if much of the time is spent in a vehicle. On these programs, the high-altitude route begins after a stop in San Pedro de Atacama, then continues through Laguna Colorada and Uyuni. Travelers with chronic conditions or previous altitude-related problems should discuss medical restrictions with a doctor before booking.

The Uruguay section, by contrast, primarily requires coordination of ferry times, border formalities and the return to Buenos Aires. The entire trip requires separate checks of entry documents by citizenship, local currencies and payment availability in every country, including those outside the highlighted selection.

## Frequently asked questions about nature in Argentina, Bolivia and Uruguay

### Are flamingo sightings in Bolivia guaranteed?

No. Laguna Colorada and other high-altitude lakes are known for flamingos, and these areas are on the itinerary. But bird numbers, viewing distances and observation conditions depend on season, weather and animal behavior.

### Will the tour visit a nature reserve in Uruguay?

On both programs discussed, the Uruguay day is spent sightseeing in Montevideo. No dedicated nature excursion in Uruguay is listed. Iguazú and the Bolivian lagoons are nature stops; the longer trip also includes a marine wildlife excursion in Ecuador's Galápagos.

### Do both tours include the Galápagos Islands?

No. The Galápagos appear only on the 32-day program as the Ecuador stage. The 20-day tour does not go there. This nature experience is not part of the selected Argentina, Bolivia and Uruguay combination.

### What preparation is needed for Laguna Colorada?

Above all, assess your altitude tolerance, pack warm clothing and protection from wind and sun, and be ready for long drives. Medical precautions are individual; a planned itinerary does not eliminate the risk of altitude sickness.

## Argentina and Brazil: which itinerary should you choose?

**For a first visit to Argentina and Brazil, a convenient foundation is Rio de Janeiro, Iguazú and Buenos Aires.** In [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), you see the ocean, Sugarloaf Mountain and Corcovado. At Iguazú, you walk along the viewing paths of two national parks. In [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), you explore neighborhoods and Argentine tango. All three stops are very different, making even a trip without Patagonia full of experiences.

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with both countries as part of the **principal** itinerary. Some programs also include Chile, Peru or Uruguay. Check the full geographical scope of each tour: a country-pair collection does not mean that every program visits only two countries.

Compare three different ways to spend your holiday.

| Option | Main idea |
|---|---|
| Rio – Iguazú – Buenos Aires | Cities and waterfalls |
| Buenos Aires – Patagonia – Iguazú – Rio | Glaciers and tropics |
| Argentina – Iguazú – Praia de Pipa | Mountains, waterfalls, beach |

The [9-day Brazil and Argentina tour](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-rio-iguazu-buenos-aires-9-days/) allocates several nights each to Rio, Iguazú and Buenos Aires. The [12-day private Ice, Sun and the End of the World itinerary](/multi-country/tour/argentina-brazil-private-tour-12-days/) includes El Calafate and Ushuaia before the waterfalls and Rio. The [11-day Praia de Pipa program](/multi-country/tour/argentina-brazil-buenos-aires-el-calafate-iguazu-pipa-11-days/) ends on Brazil's Atlantic coast.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_mechty_sbyvayutsya_tur_v_braziliyu_i_argentinu_na_9_dnej,tour_source_led_solntse_i_kraj_zemli,tour_argentina_brazil_pipa_11d}}

## Iguazú: one waterfall system, two countries and two parks

Iguazú is the natural link between the countries, but visitors make **two separate park visits**. From the Brazilian side via [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/), the broad panorama of the falls is especially impressive. From the Argentine side via [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/), walking trails lead closer to individual cascades. Both protected areas are separately listed as UNESCO World Heritage sites.

There is an international border between the parks. Traveling from one to the other is not the same as walking between two viewing platforms. Allow for driving time, immigration formalities and each park's admission rules. Access to individual trails may change because of water levels and infrastructure conditions.

The airports have different codes: **IGU** is on the Brazilian side at Foz do Iguaçu, while **IGR** serves Puerto Iguazú in Argentina. When booking the next flight, check which side of the border it departs from. Choosing the wrong airport can turn a short connection into an additional border crossing.

We plan the sequence of waterfall visits around the itinerary and subsequent flight, coordinate ground transportation and allow time for formalities. We also clarify which excursions are included: mentioning both countries in the title does not in itself confirm visits to both national parks.

## Flights, airports and border crossings

There is no compulsory order for Rio–Iguazú–Buenos Aires. If the journey starts in Brazil, it makes sense to begin in Rio, visit the waterfalls and then fly to Argentina. If the route includes [El Calafate](/argentina/place/el-calafate/) or [Ushuaia](/argentina/place/ushuaia/), the sequence also depends on domestic flights, trip duration and time available in the south.

Consider not only flight time but **the entire hotel-to-hotel journey**. In Buenos Aires, it is especially important to distinguish Ezeiza (EZE) from Jorge Newbery Aeroparque (AEP). Transferring between them requires an overland journey through the city. In Rio, international Galeão (GIG) and Santos Dumont (SDU) are also in different locations. Route convenience depends on actual tickets, not a line on a map.

If flights from Russia or another departure country connect through a third state, check **transit rules for the traveler's citizenship**. Whether visa-free transit, baggage collection and rechecking are possible depends on the airport, single or separate tickets and entry rights in the transit country. We help match flight connections to the land itinerary; final carrier arrangements and conditions must be verified before booking.

For a short vacation, limiting the journey to three major stops can be useful. A trip with Patagonia deserves more days: a domestic flight south and the return toward Iguazú take time that cannot be counted as full sightseeing days.

## Documents and entry: checking by citizenship

**For Russian citizens traveling as tourists on ordinary international passports, Argentina and Brazil have separate visa-waiver agreements.** Under each country's published official rules, short stays are permitted for up to 90 days within a 180-day period. These limits apply to each country individually, not to a combined “South American” allowance. For repeated entries, take previously spent days into account.

Before buying international flights, check passport validity, onward or return-ticket requirements, accommodation confirmation, medical coverage and transit-airport rules. Argentine legislation provides for health insurance for arriving foreign visitors; travelers should carry proof of coverage for the entire itinerary. For children, check their own documents and the conditions for traveling with accompanying adults.

Visa rules may differ in both countries for travelers of other citizenships. We begin with participants' passports, their entry sequence and transit connections, then review official requirements for the specific trip. No tour operator can guarantee a border officer's decision.

## Two currencies and practical payment methods

Argentina uses the **Argentine peso (ARS)**, while Brazil uses the **Brazilian real (BRL)**. US dollars may be useful for exchange but should not be assumed accepted for everyday purchases, taxis and admission tickets. Conversion conditions, ATM fees and payment methods vary by country and service.

Travelers with bank cards issued in Russia need particular care. Visa and Mastercard issued by Russian banks do not work abroad through those payment networks. **Foreign-issued cards must also be checked individually**: country of issue, international transaction permissions, the issuing bank and limits all matter. Do not rely on a single card or assume that dollar payments will be accepted everywhere.

Divide expenses into three groups: services prepaid under the itinerary, everyday payments on location and an emergency cash reserve in case a terminal declines a card. Before flying, establish which expenses will require Argentine pesos or Brazilian reais. We can help plan the sequence of payments and explain where it may be convenient to obtain local currency along the way, but cannot promise currency exchange or acceptance of any particular card.

## Weather: tropics, a major city and glaciers

These two countries do not share one ideal season for every itinerary. During the Southern Hemisphere summer, approximately December through February, Rio is hot and humid and Iguazú may also experience heavy rain. Buenos Aires can be hot at this time. On the other hand, it is a prime period for visiting glaciers and walking in southern Patagonia, although wind and rapid weather changes remain common.

**A Patagonia itinerary determines your clothing requirements even if the trip ends at the beach.** Pack a warm windproof and waterproof jacket, sturdy boots and light clothes for subtropical areas. For Iguazú, bring rain protection and shoes suited to wet paths. Check luggage weights and allowances against your actual domestic flight tickets.

If Rio, Iguazú and Argentina's capital are the main goals, travel dates can be more flexible. If Patagonia is important, choose the season for the south first, then optimize the Brazilian part. For a deeper exploration of one country, compare [Argentina tours](/argentina/tour/) and [Brazil tours](/brazil/tour/): fewer transfers can sometimes mean more time at the main sights.

## Frequently asked questions

### Can I see both sides of Iguazú Falls in one day?

Sometimes this is technically possible, but it depends on park hours, border queues, transfers and the chosen excursions. For unhurried visits, treat them as two separate activities rather than automatically squeezing them into a few hours.

### Do Russians need separate visas for Argentina and Brazil?

Short tourist visits with an ordinary Russian passport are covered by visa-waiver agreements with both countries, with the length of stay calculated separately in each. Check the precise rules, transit conditions and documents before departure.

### For 9–10 days, should I choose Patagonia or Rio and Iguazú?

For a first visit to both countries without many domestic flights, Rio, Iguazú and Buenos Aires are the more convenient combination. Add Patagonia when glaciers and southern landscapes matter more than free time in the cities.

### Can I pay in Argentina and Brazil with a Russian bank card?

Do not rely on Visa or Mastercard issued by Russian banks. Check a working foreign-issued card, cash and specific payment methods for the chosen program; having US dollars does not guarantee you can use them to pay everywhere.

### What changes if a third country is added?

The immigration sequence, flights and time at each stop all change. For example, [Brazil, Argentina and Chile](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile/) adds Santiago to the classic route. That program also appears in this collection because both original countries remain part of the principal journey.

## Seasons and equipment for different climate zones

Iguazú is warm and humid for much of the year; a raincoat, non-slip shoes and protection for electronics are useful. Even during the Southern Hemisphere summer, Argentine Patagonia may be windy and cold, so bring warm layers and a windproof jacket. Longer itineraries through [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/) add dry high-altitude air, while [Torres del Paine](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/) brings changeable Patagonian weather.

Local spring and summer are generally the most convenient seasons for many overland excursions in southern Patagonia. Iguazú can be visited in different months, but access to individual trails depends on water levels. In September 2026, the administration of the Argentine park reported that some walkways near Devil's Throat had been temporarily removed because of flooding. Check the condition of specific routes before traveling rather than assuming that every viewpoint is always open.

If high-altitude excursions are included, discuss preparation and any health restrictions in advance. A viewpoint visit and a substantial mountain hike require different equipment.

## The border at Iguazú and travel documents

Foz do Iguaçu and Puerto Iguazú lie in different countries. Visiting both sides of the falls is a genuine international border crossing; allow time for formalities, the road, separate tickets and possible queues.

According to official information from the Brazilian embassy checked on October 16, 2026, Russian citizens may visit Brazil for short-term tourism without a visa for up to 90 days within any 180-day period. A separate bilateral agreement with Russia applies in Argentina. Conditions for other passports, transit countries and additional countries on the itinerary must be checked individually. One visa-waiver rule does not automatically apply to all of South America.

Brazil uses the real and Argentina the peso. Chile, Bolivia or Peru require other payment arrangements. Russian-issued cards connected to international payment networks should not automatically be assumed to work abroad. Before departing, establish what has been paid to the organizer and which local expenses remain.

When traveling to Brazilian areas with yellow-fever risk, the country's Ministry of Health recommends assessing vaccination needs in advance. Medical recommendations and a formal requirement to show a certificate at entry are separate questions. Vaccination decisions should be made with a doctor according to the actual itinerary.

If waterfalls and glaciers interest you most, leave additional days for those natural regions. Adding Atacama and Bolivia broadens the geography but increases the number of flights and road transfers. ## Frequently asked questions

### Can I see both sides of Iguazú in one day?

Sometimes, yes, but the international border and park restrictions may take longer than expected. Leave some extra time for a thorough visit.

### Is glacier trekking included in every tour to Perito Moreno?

No. Viewing platforms and walking on the ice are different kinds of excursions. Check the specific itinerary.

### Do I need athletic training?

Ordinary sightseeing boardwalks and city tours have different demands from a long hike or high-altitude activity. The label “Adventure” does not indicate the difficulty level.

### When is it worth adding Chile?

When Atacama or Torres del Paine appeal to you and you have time for additional transfers. On a short holiday, a two-country route leaves more time for Iguazú and Argentina's landscapes.
